title: driver-sql MySQL: a TEXT column's declared default is still lost on three paths (NOW() default, relax/tighten MODIFY, default change)
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · os-alice · session_011y7As6JrAPNfuwC2RLXXGu

Found while fixing p0 #37320 (PR #37331; dev report #37320 comment 7169952468, `out_of_scope_findings`). One close-out card for the family: on MySQL, knex drops every DEFAULT on a `text` builder and MySQL refuses a literal DEFAULT on TEXT, so a TEXT column only keeps a default through the expression form `DEFAULT ('…')`. PR #37331 uses that form on ADD COLUMN with a literal default. Three paths still lose it:

1. A text field declaring `defaultValue: 'NOW()'` gets no column DEFAULT on MySQL (knex drops CURRENT_TIMESTAMP on TEXT; a bare one is refused). Reached by no current case.
2. The MySQL `relax_not_null` / `tighten_not_null` arms of `applyDriftOpInPlace` restate the column via `MODIFY` without its DEFAULT, so a later tighten would drop the new TEXT expression default. Read-only inference, not exercised.
3. A declared-default change on a MySQL TEXT column is not restated (the differ reads the expression form as an expression; `ALTER COLUMN SET DEFAULT` is refused on TEXT). Tables created before PR #37331 carry no DEFAULT and nothing reports it.

Re-check after PR #37331 merges: `grep -n "specificType(name, 'text')" packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/*.ts` and read `applyDriftOpInPlace`'s MySQL arms.

Responsibility: platform code, `packages/drivers/driver-sql` (this repo); no platform path covers these today; reached by a MySQL deployment whose objects declare defaults on text fields (path 2 and 3 on schema change).
